title: We Keep Hearing About AI Productivity. The QA Group Chat Told a Different Story.
why_read: An anecdotal but relatable piece about QA professionals' anxieties and experiences with AI-driven testing changes, offering a useful counter-narrative to AI productivity hype.
analysis: This article reports on informal, unscientific polling within a QA community group where a notable fraction of members reported being unemployed, implicitly linking it to AI's effect on QA jobs and workflows. It raises a real and discussed issue in software testing: that automating QA work exposes previously hidden manual workarounds and inconsistent requirements documents. The evidence here is anecdotal rather than rigorous, essentially a Dev.to blog post built around a Slack-style poll rather than any formal study. Still, the underlying tension, automation revealing organizational dysfunction, is a genuine and valuable observation for engineering managers and QA practitioners.
